title: Navi Mumbai Airport Goes International With First Abu Dhabi Flight as India-UAE Air Corridor Expands
excerpt: Air India Express launched the first overseas service from India's newest greenfield airport, connecting the Mumbai Metropolitan Region to Abu Dhabi three times a week and opening a second international gateway for the country's commercial capital.
body:
• Air India Express operated Navi Mumbai International Airport's first international flight to Abu Dhabi on July 15, carrying around 100 passengers on a Boeing 737 MAX 8.
  • The airport, which opened for domestic flights on December 25, 2025, has already connected 46 Indian cities and handled over 2.3 million passengers in under seven months.
  • Abu Dhabi's Zayed International Airport will expand direct connectivity to 22 Indian cities by August, up from 17, with Indian passengers accounting for 24 percent of total airport traffic.
  • The Tata Group-owned airline also launched new Abu Dhabi services from Indore and Lucknow the same week, with Guwahati to follow next month.

From Domestic Hub to International Gateway

Navi Mumbai International Airport has crossed a major milestone with its first scheduled international passenger service, an Air India Express flight to Abu Dhabi that took off at 2:55 AM IST on July 15 and landed in the UAE capital roughly two-and-a-half hours later.

The flight carried around 100 passengers, including families heading onward to Muscat and business travelers bound for the Gulf. It also transported the airport's first global shipment of perishable cargo, opening a new trade corridor for exporters across Maharashtra and western India.

The Adani Group-owned airport — in which Maharashtra's urban planning agency Cidco holds a 26 percent stake — began domestic commercial operations on December 25, 2025, after being inaugurated by Prime Minister Narendra Modi the previous October. In fewer than 200 days, it went from handling its first domestic passenger to launching overseas service.

A Second Gateway for Mumbai

The Abu Dhabi route addresses a practical problem for millions of travelers. For residents of Navi Mumbai, Thane, Panvel, and the eastern suburbs, Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj International Airport in western Mumbai has long meant a grueling cross-city commute before the journey even begins. The new airport creates a second international departure point on the other side of the metropolitan region.

Air India Express Chairman Nipun Aggarwal described Navi Mumbai as "a key pillar of its dual-airport strategy," complementing the carrier's existing network from Mumbai's main international hub. The airline now operates 30 weekly flights from Navi Mumbai, connecting the airport to Abu Dhabi, Bengaluru, and Delhi.

"We are running out of traffic rights. Demand for additional capacity and more destinations continues to increase."

— Carsten Norland, Chief Commercial Officer, Abu Dhabi Airports

India-UAE Demand Surges

The launch taps into one of the strongest air travel corridors in the region. Abu Dhabi Airports Chief Commercial Officer Carsten Norland said Indian passenger traffic accounts for nearly 7 million travelers annually — 24 percent of the airport's overall traffic. Of those, about 5 million are point-to-point passengers and 2 million use Abu Dhabi as a transit hub for connections to Europe, Africa, and elsewhere.

Zayed International Airport will expand its direct India network to 22 cities by August, up from 17, Norland said at a panel discussion marking the Air India Express launch. The airline also started Abu Dhabi services from Indore and Lucknow the same week, with Guwahati scheduled to follow next month.

Haitham Al Khamis, Director of Tourism Product Development at Abu Dhabi's Department of Culture and Tourism, described India as "one of Abu Dhabi's most important tourism markets and a strategic partner," supported by strong business links and the large Indian diaspora in the UAE.

What's Next

With 46 domestic destinations, over 2.3 million passengers served, and approximately 150 air traffic movements daily, Navi Mumbai has built the operational foundation to support a broader international network. More overseas routes are expected as additional carriers evaluate the airport's growing passenger base.

For the 3.5 million Indians living in the UAE and the millions more who travel there annually for work, tourism, and family visits, the expanded connectivity means more options, shorter commutes to the airport, and potentially more competitive fares as airlines compete for a share of one of India's busiest international travel markets.
